## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven: 2 (average). Go here.** Boats found Chinook and steelhead 40 to 90 feet down in 80 to 160 feet of water. Run orange, green, or blue spoons at those depths.
- **St. Joseph: 1 (below average).** Boats were fishing inside 70 feet, and the report called the fishing inconsistent. Fish deeper than that if you go.
- **South Haven: 1 (below average).** Only a few boats went out. Try 60 to 100 feet of water with spoons, and expect small fish.
- **Muskegon: 1 (below average).** Boats fished only "when the weather allowed." Orange spoons worked in 70 to 140 feet of water. Muskegon is the fallback if Grand Haven is too rough.
- **My pick: Grand Haven.** Check the wind before you launch from any of these ports.

## Why

- Grand Haven gets the top rating because its latest boat report is the most detailed, with depths, fish depth, and lures that worked (Grand Haven, 2025-10-09).
- St. Joseph and South Haven rank lower because their latest boat reports were rated 1, below average (St. Joseph, 2025-10-09; South Haven, 2025-10-09).
- I'd expect the bite to stay in the deeper water. Boats did best beyond 100 feet in late September (St. Joseph, 2025-09-24), and similar cool-water weeks in past years were slow near shore (South Haven, 2024-10-23).
- Upwelling wind was frequent last week, with 24 to 34 hours of north-to-east wind (all four ports, 2025-10-09). That can help the bite, but it also means rough water for a small boat.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2025-10-09, five days old)
- Grand Haven, 2025-10-09: "Boat anglers found immature Chinook salmon and steelhead 40 to 90 feet down in 80 to 160 feet of water… A mix of orange, green, and blue spoons worked well." Quality not rated. The pier was "slow" (quality 0).
- Muskegon, 2025-10-09: "When the weather allowed, boat anglers found steelhead and immature salmon in 70 to 140 feet of water… Orange spoons worked well." Quality not rated. Gusts reached 33 mph.
- South Haven, 2025-10-09: "The few boats that made it out were fishing in 60 feet of water out to 100 feet…" Coho and small Chinook were caught on spoons. Quality 1 for both.
- St. Joseph, 2025-10-09: "Salmon fishing was very inconsistent this week… Fishing was reported to be either very good or very poor." Boats fished inside 70 feet. Quality 1.
- Prior week, 2025-10-01: Grand Haven boats fished 70 to 150 feet with spoons, quality not rated. South Haven boats were rated 2 (fair, scattered fish). St. Joseph boats were rated 2 at 80+ feet. Muskegon boats were rated 2 farther out and 0 in the basin.

**Past seasons** (history, not current conditions)
- Weeks with similar surface water (about 61 F) were mostly slow to average for boats. South Haven, 2024-10-23: "slow fishing… the best fishing was reported to have been in very deep water." Grand Haven, 2024-10-02: boats rated 2 at 30 to 90 feet down, with orange spoons.
- In 2023, the South Haven piers were closed due to poor weather (South Haven, 2023-10-11).

**Conditions now**
- The live conditions data was unavailable. The tool returned a backtest summary for the week before October 14, showing buoy surface water of about 58 to 63 F across the four ports. I did not use it to rate the ports.
- I don't have this weekend's wind forecast.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from 2025-10-09, five days old. Conditions can change quickly this time of year.
- Live water temperature and the wind forecast were unavailable, so I couldn't check today's upwelling or the wind for the trip. Check the forecast before you launch.
- Several ratings rest on unrated reports (Grand Haven and Muskegon). A "not rated" report means fish were caught but the quality wasn't stated, so I treated it as a weak positive.
- The ratings are my judgment from one or two reports per port, not a measured catch rate.
